reviews.comment: Dr. Karmakar is a decent professor and teaches well, just make sure to go to class and listen to lecture. All tests are open note, but you will not get it if you don't do the practice questions she provides! Those really helped me on the exams. Overall, this was a good but a bit boring course, if you need the credit though I'd definitely take her!

Exams and quizzes are all open note. Everything is very doable given a small understanding of whats going on with some sample code to look at. It is clear that she wants her students to succeed and get a high grade. My only complaint is occasionally there may be typos in grading keys, but she ensures that you will get the points you deserve.

She can be hard to understand in lectures but as long as you follow along with her code and review the stat terms in her PowerPoints you'll be fine. there's usually typos in assignments that results in some points back. She is good at explaining questions in office hours.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I do not understand some of these 211 reviews. I barely paid attention, although I usually attended the class, and got a high A. Homework has 10 attempts each so guaranteed 100% there, quizzes aren't hard and exams are the same as the test review problems just rephrased/different numbers, and you get a cheat sheet on all exams including the final.

Her lectures were hard to follow and didn't help very much. I recommend studying her powerpoints and understanding her homeworks and quizzes. Exams were fine but always had something that we did not learn. Many of her homeworks, quizzes, and exams were keyed wrong so definitely look over what you missed and email her about it.

Talks really fast and lectures were a little confusing, but overall, not a bad professor. She's a relatively new professor trying to work out the quirks of the class but she tries really hard and offers extra office hours and personally holds review sessions.3 MCQ test total, each question worth 1% of your grade(70%), tests very similar to reviews.

I agree with the review that calls you a wimp if you complain. It is very clear whats asked of you in this course. Karmakar is by no means unfair or overly difficult. Stats is a tough class and if you get this prof dont panic. Study the reviews and homeworks and quizes, exam questions are recycled from those. You got this, if got an A so can you.

Attendance is not mandatory, but seeing how she goes through the code is helpful. Only a few quizzes and homework, and would not really tell you how to calculate your grade. Just that cavas isn't accurate. She only talked about that in office hours, as well. Did not announce to the whole class. Also reopened the quizzes at the end of the semester.

she mumbles so hard to understand. content itself is not difficult, but she confuses people. her reviews, hw, quizzes, and exams always have mistakes so they usually had to be regraded which causes people more stress. canvas grade is wrong so you will not know what your overall grade is because she will also not tell you how to calculate it

Her class is very straightforward There are only 8 short homework assignments and you are given 2 weeks to do them with 10 attempts, the quizzes are almost always problems we've gone over in class. Her exams are very similar to the review. She gave extra credit. Anyone complaining is a wimp. She is miles better than all other engineering profs.

She always makes mistakes in review materials, and most of them will make you fell super confused. Her homework and quizzes make it easy to gain grades, but if you haven't learned stats before, avoid her.

Her lectures aren't great, her slides aren't that bad but can be all over the place and hard to study but most recently she has been better. One major problem is that she will often make mistakes and never notice them in class and especially in answer keys for practice problems. It is hard to study correctly when the teacher is doing it wrong.

Professor Karmakar does not have the best lectures but she is fair to her students. Her exams are very similar to the practice sets she provides, so as long as you study those heavily, you will do well in the class. The quizzes and homeworks were not an issue for me as there were large windows to submit them.

Mixed emotions about this prof, her lectures are terrible and completely irrelevant altogether, but she gives you lots of help with study material and makes the exams very similar to practice problems. All 3 tests including the final had significant grading mistakes, which just caused unnecessary stress for everyone. Accessible outside of class tho

Lectures never felt welcoming. The ONLY thing that helps in this class somewhat is the Rscripts she posts which essentially give the answers to all the questions, but sometimes incorrect. One time she gave us an exam question that was word for word one of the problems with the solution on the script, and yet somehow i still got half credit.

the key for every assignment and exam had many mistakes. TA graded the longer assignments, which we never got rubrics for. she never told us how to calculate  grade (the canvas one was inaccurate). lectures are monotone and confusing. slides were hard to follow. canvas modules were very unorganized.  easy class but she makes it hard to follow.

(STAT 312) Absolutely awful. Worst professor I've had by far at TAMU. Incomprehensible lectures and tests are poorly structured. The answer key on the last test was completely wrong and she had to change it an hour later. If you want to have a fair class that reflects the effort you put into it, stay away from her.

in-person lectures are incomprehensible, dont go as they will confuse you more than help you. The problem with that is the test review material is more than half incorrect, those also confuse you more than help you. Ur going to teach this class to yourself. Also,the use of R is the most irrelevant thing I have ever done in a class. She doesn't care

The most recent reviews basically sum everything up. She posts her materials but almost all of it is wrong. Nice person but none of her material will help you study or understand. The "probability" of getting it wrong from using her work is about... 95%.

Test reviews and HW are full of wrong answers so trying to use her material to study will only cause you to fail bc once again, all wrong. HW is often opened again because of mistakes and will round answers weird so if you solve the problems exactly you will get the wrong answer. Will go back & fix mistakes and will not even completely fix them all

Karmakar is a nice person, but really can't teach. Going to lectures is pointless. She never smiles. She seems like she hates stats. All the homework's have errors. She mumbles. It's interesting because I leave class knowing less than when I came in. My kindergarten teacher could make Statistics more comprehensible than Karmakar. Nice person though

She does not give a lot of homework in general, but when we do have assignments the answer key is either WRONG or she gives a zero percent error for free response questions. Exams are 20 questions each and all MC. Solutions she gives for practice problems/exam reviews are almost always wrong as well. Do not recommend!

Big yapper. Gets up in front of class and just blabbers incoherently. Questions aren't even that hard, she just manages to explain them so poorly they become confusing. Problems would make more sense if she just put them up on screen and left.

Honestly, I don't have much to say about Professor Karmakar. If you've taken a stats class before, you are probably fine. She's not great at teaching, and the exam reviews she gives out sometimes have the wrong answers. She gives off the impression that she's bored and has better places to be. The coding assignments are a joke that no else does.

She is a very nice person, but as a lecturer not very good. I stopped going to class and did just fine. Make sure to do well on the tests because the final does not replace the lowest. Homework is very easy to keep up with. If you took stats in highschool you should get an easy B and just study before the exams and you should get an A.

(Stat 312) It definitely helps to have previous understanding of stats, I took STAT 201 before and that was basically everything before the midterm. I've never coded before so everything being in R was hard. She goes through the slides fast but is good about stopping and re-explaining slower something if someone asks or if everyone looks confused
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I literally went to maybe 10 classes max and got a B. Thank god class is optional because her lectures are absolutely atrocious and her slides are just as bad. If you took AP stats in high school, its an easy B and with a little effort an A.

(STAT 312). I enjoyed her teaching style as she was very thorough and did a lot of examples that were similar to the material I would see on exams and homework. Attendance is not mandatory but she offered some in-class practices that could only be done if you were in person. Also offered a lot of extra credit. Good experience.

Her slides are lengthy and unorganized. There are no quizzes and the 3 tests are 20 questions, no partial credit. She does not respond to emails. Was really upsetting to hear that most other STAT 211 professors allowed open note and online for their tests, when our class was working so hard and teaching everything to ourselves on our own.

AVOID this professor at all costs. ALL other STAT211 professors r better. Exams r closed notes & all the other professors allow you to use your notes. Moves super quickly & is extremely disorganized. Grades are not graded until the last minute & are mostly based on exams, worth 65%. so if u r a bad test taker like me don't take her you will fail.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Half the class is about to receive a zero on an assignment because she misplaced an attendance sheet, very ditzy.
Most disorganized professor I have ever had. Nice lady, but awful professor. She makes coding much more difficult than it should be. Lectures confuse you more than it helps.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are really hard to focus on but really try bc they are important. In order to prepare for the exams redo hw and quiz problems and the problems in the slides. The "practice exam questions" aren't that helpful ironically. This class is doable as long as you practice enough, I would say she's a decent and fair prof.

While she reopened all the homework and all of the quizzes for us to retake which is basically built-in extra credit, all of her lectures were kind of hard to follow. It didn't help that they were online though. Had to do a lot of work outside of class to learn the material. She gives practice tests! I don't know if other profs are better.

She means well, but man her lectures are brutal. She will confuse you on the simplest concepts. Basically a teach yourself course. Scatterbrained on what material to put on exams. Practice exams don't prepare you well for the actual exams, and both of them have errors in her calculations and spelling. Listen closely and practice the hw's.

Gives a lot of resources to help study for test. Tests are doable, and some questions on test were similar to hw or quizzes. Lectures were 1.25hrs and can be hard to focus. She lectures at a good pace, but will not go back often because she posts the lectures for you to review. Key to an A is to do as many practice problems as you can.

Her online lectures are mediocre and difficult to follow. YouTube is the reason I have an A in the course. Weekly homework and quizzes, similar to exam problems. 2 MC lecture exams and a final. She has practice exams, although the first practice exam was not helpful at all. She has the best grade distribution for STAT302, so pick her if you can.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: No textbook req'd. 1 hr of video lecture every day. The video lectures were recycled from a different prof. 5 years ago. Dr. Karmakar didn't teach except for live Q&A sessions, during which it was difficult to tell if she knew the material herself. I know there was a huge grading curve: I don't understand any of the material, but I still got an A.

it's just antagonizing, painful experience online. I'm writing this to forewarn future students, staying awake during her online lectures is harder than the class material itself. Do yourself a favor a take w/ a more engaging prof. You'll thank me later. She did curve tho so props to her for that. But she is just so bland during PPs.

This class is probably my biggest regret. The weekly homeworks are INSANE, even for a master's class. You'll probably spend 10 hours on each. Granted she does give hints and has a Q&A session, but so much material still goes uncovered. It's basically a DIY class because she doesn't lecture (prerecorded from the previous prof)... goodluck lol

I'm truly confused about some of the previous comments, because there was no extra credit or high test averages in Dr. Karmakar's class. I struggled intensely for an A, and I'd say I'm relatively good at math. I would tune out her lectures and teach myself bc she honestly confused me and it was easier that way. Nice lady, but not a great prof.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I could not stand her or her class. Yes she was nice face to face, but she was so unorganized and scatterbrained it ended up confusing me on easy material. Her final was all messed up online and she really didn't seem to care at all. She promised to curve, I was not curved and when I brought it up she ghosted me. I would not suggest her to anyone

I want to give her some benefit of the doubt b/c covid but I just cannot. She is an awfully organized lecturer and grader alike. I just took my final and it was filled with so many errors, this class was unbearable with this prof. Stay away if you know whats good for your gpa. 0/5 if I could She rambles so GD much in lecture, 30 min per example.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Karmakar is a solid choice for stats. There are in-class participation questions, so going to class was helpful. She posts lots of practice problems and hosts many review sessions before exams.
Dr. Karmakar really is a great professor!! She really cares for her students and is always ready to help! she explains everything so well and always wants to help! take her!!!
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She means well, but she is pretty bad at explaining stats if you are confused. I took AP Stats in high school, so I knew all of the information covered, but I could tell other students were struggling with understanding her. Easy tests and homeworks, but if you are confused, find someone that understands stats because she will only make it worse.
She is amazing if you go to class and pay attention to the lectures you will be fine. You will definitely learn statistics after this class.

easiest prof Ive taken at A&M. I barely studied and got 105s on all the exams, plus she gives so much extra credit. 10/10 would recommend if you dont actually want to learn statistics and just want an A.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is so nice and genuinely cares about the students. Shes accessible outside of class and holds review sessions for each test if you need extra help. But Honestly, her teaching wasnt very effective for me. Shed take 20 minutes to solve a problem that should take 3 minutes so Id zone out. I was better off going over notes at home. Not hard tho

Would not recommend for graduate or online courses. Slow to respond to questions (several days), didn't take time to understand student questions, sometimes only seemed to know as much as was in the posted solutions. Thankfully, notes, lecture videos, and presumably assignments and tests, were from a previous semester with a different professor.
Has notes online but still went to every lecture because she was was good at explaining, would take again
reviews.ratingTags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This professor truly gave her students every opportunity to do well. People that complain about her truly did not put in the minimal effort required to make an A in this course. She really cares about her students and wanted us to do well all semester long. If you have the chance to take her, TAKE HER!

Her exams are literally the Problem Sets she gives you to prepare for the exam with different numbers. The MEDIAN on our first exam was a 100. Basically let us retake every quiz with the correct answers for full credit back and generally posted the answers to homework before it was due. I showed up to class only for exams and made a straight 100.
reviews.ratingTags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: LOTS of issues with figuring out what the correct answer is on homework, test reviews, and in class problems because she will show us one thing and then expect another. Tests were easy but you have to teach yourself how to do it. Don't learn much in class so there is no point in going because you learn on your own or else you are in trouble.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Quizzes every week counts as attendance, very easy class she gives lots of makeup grades. Tests are short and easy just like the practice questions. She gets confused a lot and nervous from the students.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This was her 1st year teaching, so maybe thats why I did so poorly. This class is extremely difficult by itself, but she is not very good at explaining difficult concepts. a student would ask a question and she would answer a different question, not the one asked. She would also solve an entire problem wrong and not realize it until the end.
